summary: Intent now formally defines ARGO-INIT-VALIDATOR-BOOTSTRAP-CONTRACT as an explicit acceptance baseline mounted under 显性测试用例. Implementation Design must materialize one read-only explicit testcase entry, align repository contracts and critical guardrails to that baseline, bootstrap the validator plus the full handoff schema set into Argo-managed .github paths, apply the chosen package.json seeding policy without overwriting conflicting scripts, and keep missing Node/npm runtime classified as an explicit prerequisite failure rather than a bootstrap responsibility.

explicitTestcases.name: ARGO-INIT-VALIDATOR-BOOTSTRAP-CONTRACT
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Invoke /argo-init in a target workspace that lacks some or all Argo validator bootstrap assets, including the validator script, the full .github/argoschema handoff schema set, and optionally package.json.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: After bootstrap, the workspace contains .github/validator/script/validateStageHandoff.js, .github/argoschema/SystemArchitecture.schema.json, .github/argoschema/IntentToImplementationHandoff.schema.json, and .github/argoschema/ImplementationToCodingHandoff.schema.json under Argo-managed paths; package.json is created when absent and otherwise only missing validate:handoff, validate:handoff:intent, and validate:handoff:implementation scripts are added, while pre-existing same-name scripts trigger conflict reporting instead of overwrite. If Node/npm is unavailable, that prerequisite failure is surfaced explicitly rather than treated as a bootstrap success.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: Implementation Design must materialize this baseline as one read-only explicit testcase entry plus the necessary bootstrap contracts and critical verification guardrails for /argo-init. Bootstrap is not permission to fabricate missing design/KG handoff JSON payloads or to overwrite conflicting existing script names.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: The explicit testcase is now formalized in design/KG/SystemArchitecture.json. The next stage should trace the physical read-only entry, command contract linkage, and critical non-explicit guardrails back to this graph-mounted baseline.

notes: This handoff now treats the testcase as a graph-owned explicit baseline rather than a handoff-only workaround.
The selected policy permits /argo-init to create a minimal package.json when absent and to seed the three validate:handoff scripts only when they are missing.
If any of the target script names already exist, Implementation Design should preserve the no-overwrite rule and require explicit conflict reporting.
Missing usable Node/npm runtime remains outside the bootstrap implementation contract and must be reported as a prerequisite failure at execution time.
